newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Nat Gas, Bay of Plenty plan cogeneration plant.
newsitem.headline: NZ Nat Gas, Bay of Plenty plan cogeneration plant.

text.p: Bay of Plenty Electricity and Natural Gas Corporation said on Friday they had reached an agreement in principle to form a joint venture for the construction of a major cogeneration facility at Kapuni, in the North Island's Taranaki region.
The plant, which will have 25 megawatt capacity and will produce 196 gigawatts of electrical energy and 492,000 tonnes of steam annually, is expected to cost NZ$30-$40 million dollars.
It will be funded by the two companies on a 50:50 basis.

The facility, to be located within the site of Natural Gas Corp's gas treatment plant at Kapuni, will meet the entire steam and electricity requirements of the gas treatment plant as well as the Lactose NZ Limited lactose plant approximately three kilometres away.
The proposal includes the construction of pipelines to carry steam to the lactose plant, and water, condensed during the process, from the Lactose plant to the cogeneration facility.
Excess electrical energy will be sold by the joint venture to Bay of Plenty Electricity for distribution to its customers.
It is hoped the facility will be completed in November 1997. --Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
